Definition: perhaps from ἄγαν (much) [or compare H5689 ]; to love (in a social or moral sense):--(be-)love(-ed). Compare G5368.
BiblicalUsage: Agapao is to love — the great word of the New Testament, used hundreds of times. Jesus commands it toward enemies, John says God so loved the world that He gave His Son, the same apostle commands believers to love one another as Christ loved them, and then states the ground of it all: God is love, and whoever does not love does not know Him. The word covers God's love for us, our love for Him, and our love for each other, and it always means love that acts.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that agapao is the word the whole gospel turns on. God loved, so He gave; Christ loved, so He died; and we love because He first loved us — and any love that does not act is not the love this word means.
